sections.what_happened: hormuz.now's Oct 27 01:03 UTC update puts AIS-visible commercial traffic through Hormuz at 7.3 crossings/day over the past week vs 84.8 pre-crisis (~9%), status 'severely restricted' since Oct 19 15:42 UTC, JMIC threat SEVERE, US-coordinated southern corridor operating, US blockade of Iranian ports active since Jul 14. hormuz.now is NOT in the source registry: its figure is an attributed tracker number, never a corroborated count. PortWatch backbone: snapshot portwatch-2026-10-26.json is STALE (latest observation 2026-10-18, 8-day lag; 7-day avg 3.7 vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day = 4.3%). The two trackers differ in method (AIS-visible commercial crossings vs PortWatch AIS calls) -- do NOT blend them; cite each with its own date and baseline. CENTCOM's competing claim (Oct 25: 3,000+ vessels assisted, 1.5bn barrels, 95% safe) remains a claimant figure, not a counted one.
sections.what_verified: No registry family corroborates the hormuz.now figure
sections.what_disputed: CENTCOM (Oct 25) says primary lanes are mine-free and 95% of ships sailed safely; Kpler data cited by Hürriyet says crude exports reached pre-war levels in September (16.5mbd ex-Iran) -- a flow-based measure, not a transit count.
sections.why_matters: Hormuz by the Numbers check: a second tracker now counts 7.3 crossings a day -- still ~9% of normal. Two trackers, same collapse, different methods; PortWatch itself is 8 days stale.
sections.context: Background: FRANCHISE DATA NOTE -- Hormuz tracker hormuz.now status update Oct 27 01:03 UTC: AIS-visible traffic 7.3/day vs 84.8 pre-crisis (~9%), 'severely restricted' since Oct 19; PortWatch backbone still STALE (Oct 18 observation)

totw_analysis: Our read: Hormuz by the Numbers check: a second tracker now counts 7.3 crossings a day -- still ~9% of normal. Two trackers, same collapse, different methods; PortWatch itself is 8 days stale. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Who counts as 'open'? CENTCOM's escorted-flow story vs AIS trackers showing ~9% of normal crossings -- the gap between escorted oil and visible traffic.
